changesOnDisk:
        watching:
            The editor watches its file on disk while it is open, whether or
            not its tab is selected, and notices when something else edits or
            renames it: another program, a task, or the @{FileTreeScope}. Its
            own saves, the formatting a Piton file gets as it is saved
            included, are never taken for a change on disk.

        reloading:
            When the file is edited on disk and the editor has no unsaved
            changes, it reloads at once, without asking, showing the file as
            it now is on disk. As with saving, the cursor stays at the same
            place in the text, beside the same characters it was beside, as
            near as the new text allows, and the view stays scrolled just as
            it was. The reload can't be undone into the text it replaced, and
            a Piton file's new text goes to the server as a full-text
            `textDocument/didChange`.

        renaming:
            When the file is renamed or moved on disk, whether the file system
            reports it as a rename or the file vanishes while one with the
            same contents appears in the project at the same moment, the
            editor follows it to its new path in the same tab: its header
            shows the new path, its tab the new name and path, and saving
            writes to the new path. Nothing else about it changes: its text,
            unsaved changes, cursor, and scrolling stay as they were, so a
            rename alone never asks anything. A Piton file is closed on the
            server under its old path with `textDocument/didClose`, and opened
            under its new one with `textDocument/didOpen`, with the editor's
            text. A rename that also changes the file's contents is a rename
            and then an edit.

        conflicts:
            When the file is edited on disk while the editor has unsaved
            changes, nothing is reloaded. Instead a dialog asks what to do,
            titled "notes.md changed on disk" with the file's name, saying the
            file was changed outside the editor while it has unsaved changes
            here, with three buttons, the last one primary:

            - "Keep Mine", which keeps the editor's text as it is, still
              unsaved, so saving it writes over what is on disk
            - "Reload", which discards the unsaved changes and reloads the
              file as it now is on disk, as reloading says
            - "Merge", which opens the merge, as merging says

            The dialog shows as soon as the change is noticed, whichever tab is
            selected, and choosing "Reload" or "Merge" selects the file's tab.
            <Escape>, or closing the dialog, is "Keep Mine". While the dialog
            is open, further changes to the file on disk don't open another;
            the choice made acts on the file as it is on disk when it is
            made. Each file in conflict gets a dialog of its own, one after
            another. A file that conflicts again after "Keep Mine" asks again.

        merging:
            "Merge" shows, in place of the editor in the file's tab, a
            @{DiffViewScope} that merges, as its merging says: the file as it
            now is on disk on its left, and the editor's unsaved text on its
            right. Applying the merge puts the merged text in the editor as
            its text, still unsaved, with the cursor and view kept as when
            reloading, so it is saved as any other change is, and the editor
            shows again. Cancelling it shows the editor again, its text as it
            was before the merge, as with "Keep Mine". While the merge shows,
            the tab still shows the unsaved dot, and closing the tab asks
            whether to discard the unsaved changes, as closing says.

    otherFiles:
        Each open file has an editor of its own.

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/application/Body import BodyScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP
from /scope/open-file import OpenFileScope
from /ui/components/file-tree import FileTreeScope
from /ui/components/selection-popover import SelectionPopoverScope

export ui-component EditorScope:
    concept: {EditorConcept}

concept EditorConcept:
    pitch:
        An editor for a file opened from the @{FileTreeScope}, or anywhere else
        the @{OpenFileScope} says, with language support for Piton files.

    shape: {EditorShape}

shape EditorShape:
    description:
        Editable and syntax highlighted, in its own tab of the @{BodyScope},
        under a header with the file's path in the project, a dot while it has
        unsaved changes, a save button, and a close button.

    layout:
        Everything in the tab is laid out the same plain way, with no stray
        padding or margin anywhere. The header runs the tab's full width, 32
        pixels tall, as tall as the body's tab bar, its contents centred up
        and down in it, with 12 pixels of padding at its left and 8 at its
        right, and a single 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its
        bottom, the only line in the tab. In it, from the left: the file's
        path, then 6 pixels after it the unsaved dot while there is one, then
        at the far right the Save button and the close button, 4 pixels
        apart. Both buttons are small ghost buttons 24 pixels tall, the
        close button an icon button 24 pixels square, neither with a border.
        The header has no margin of its own above, below, or beside it: it
        starts at the top of the tab, directly beneath the tab bar, and its
        left and right edges are the tab's.

        Beneath the header, the file fills the rest of the tab edge to edge,
        with no margin, border, or rounded corner around it, and nothing
        between it and the header's line. Its text starts 12 pixels in from
        the tab's left edge, the same as the path in the header above it, so
        the two line up, and 8 pixels below the header's line. A message that
        the file can't be read, or can't be saved, is set in by the same 12
        pixels, in a row as tall as its text needs with 8 pixels above and
        below it.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Every file is highlighted in its language, using the grammars gpui-kit's
        editor comes with: Piton, and Astro, Bash, C, C++, C#, CMake, CSS,
        diffs, EJS, Elixir, ERB, Go, GraphQL, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSON,
        Kotlin, Lua, Make, Markdown, PHP, Protocol Buffers, Python, Ruby, Rust,
        Scala, Svelte, Swift, TOML, TSX, TypeScript, YAML, and Zig. SQL is left
        out, as its grammar can't be built alongside gpui.

        The language comes from the file's extension, ignoring case, including
        the other extensions a language goes by, such as .h for C, .hpp and .cc
        for C++, .jsx, .mjs, and .cjs for JavaScript, .mts and .cts for
        TypeScript, .htm for HTML, .exs for Elixir, .zsh for Bash, .yml for
        YAML, and .scss, .sass, and .less for CSS. Some files are known by their
        whole name instead: Makefile for Make, CMakeLists.txt for CMake,
        Cargo.lock for TOML, Gemfile and Rakefile for Ruby, and shell startup
        files like .bashrc and .zshrc for Bash. A file in any other language, or
        with no extension, is plain text.

    selectingText:
        Selecting text in the editor by dragging across it shows a
        @{SelectionPopoverScope} with four buttons:
        - Cut, with a scissors icon, which puts the selected text on the clipboard and removes it from the file
        - Copy, with a copy icon, which puts the selected text on the clipboard
        - Paste, with a clipboard icon, which puts what is on the clipboard in place of the selected text
        - Send to Prompt, with a paperclip icon, which attaches the selected text to the prompt, as attaching text selected in an answer does

        Cut, Copy, and Paste do just what their shortcuts do in the editor, and
        can be undone the same way. Cut and Paste are disabled while the file
        can't be edited yet. After any of them the editor keeps focus. The
        popover also closes when the text changes, or when the file closes.

    ruler:
        A thin vertical line, in the theme's line colour, runs down the text at
        the 80th column, the width a line should keep within. Past it, the
        editor's background is a step darker than the well, as black laid over
        it, 25% in dark mode and 5% in light mode, so text running long stands
        out while staying as readable. The line and the shade scroll sideways
        with the text, are drawn behind it, and never take the mouse.

    keyboard:
        indentation:
            A tab stop is 4 spaces: <Tab> indents by 4 spaces, <Shift+Tab>
            outdents by 4, and a new line's indentation counts in 4s.

        backspace:
            <Backspace> with nothing selected, when everything between the
            start of the line and the cursor is spaces, deletes back to the
            tab stop before the cursor, up to 4 spaces at once, as though the
            indentation were tabs. Anywhere else, or with a selection, it
            deletes as ever, a character or the selection.

        home:
            The editor moves about a line the way a good code editor does.
            <Home> goes to the line's first character that isn't whitespace;
            pressed again there, or on a line that is only whitespace, it goes
            to the very start of the line, and pressed again from there, back
            to its first character. With <Shift> it selects the same way.

        newLines:
            <Enter> starts the new line at the indentation of the line it
            breaks, as the language's indentation rules say. On a line that is
            an item of a Markdown or Piton list, starting with a dash, an
            asterisk, or a plus and a space, or a number and a period and a
            space, the new line starts a new item of the same list at the same
            indentation, a numbered item counting on from the one before.
            <Enter> on an item with nothing after its marker ends the list
            instead: the marker is taken away, leaving the line empty at its
            indentation. <Enter> with an open completion or quick fix menu is
            the menu's.

    newFiles:
        The editor can also show a file that isn't on disk yet, starting with
        the text it is given. It has unsaved changes from the start, and saving
        it writes it, making its folders as needed.

    saving:
        Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) or the save button writes the file to disk. A
        file that cannot be saved keeps its changes and says why beneath the
        header.

        Saving never moves the cursor or the view. A Piton file is formatted
        as it is saved, and the editor then shows the formatted text, with the
        cursor still at the same place in the text, beside the same characters
        it was beside, and scrolled just as it was.

    languageSupport:
        overview:
            A Piton file (`.pi`) is edited with the project's @{LSP} server,
            shared with the chat input, which sees the editor's unsaved text:
            the file is opened with `textDocument/didOpen`, kept current with
            full-text `textDocument/didChange`, reported with
            `textDocument/didSave` when saved, and closed with
            `textDocument/didClose` when the editor closes or shows another
            file. Other files are edited without language support, as is a Piton
            file while the server is not running.

        completions:
            `textDocument/completion` is requested after typing a letter, a
            digit, an opening curly brace, a period, a dollar sign, an at sign,
            a colon, or an underscore, and narrowed and ordered as in the chat
            input. Accepting a completion also applies the import the server
            attaches to it.

        hover:
            Hovering a name shows the server's `textDocument/hover`. Typing in
            the editor clears whatever the pointer's hover shows, the name's
            hover and a diagnostic's message alike, as soon as a key changes
            the text, and nothing hovered shows again until the pointer next
            moves over the text.

        definitions:
            Ctrl-clicking (Cmd-clicking on macOS) a name goes to its
            `textDocument/definition`. A definition in another file opens that
            file at the definition, as the @{OpenFileScope} says.

        diagnostics:
            What the server publishes for the file is underlined, with the
            message shown on hover, and kept while the text is edited until the
            server publishes again.

        quickFixes:
            Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on macOS) lists the server's `textDocument/codeAction`
            fixes at the cursor, and picking one applies its edits to the file.

    otherFiles:
        Each open file has an editor of its own. Opening another file opens
        it in another tab, leaving this one as it is, its unsaved changes,
        cursor, and scrolling kept for when its tab is selected again.

    closing:
        The close button above the file, or the one on its tab, closes it.
        While there are unsaved changes, it first asks whether to discard
        them.

use /lib
use /ui

from /scope/git import GitScope

export panel FileTreeScope:
    height: fill
    scrolls: true

    concept: {FileTreeConcept}

concept FileTreeConcept:
    pitch:
        A tree view of the files and folders in the current
        @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, for finding a file and opening it.

    shape: {FileTreeShape}

shape FileTreeShape:
    description:
        Folders are listed before files, both by name, and a folder's contents
        are shown when it is expanded. It scrolls with a @{ScrollbarScope}.
        Until a project is picked it reads "No project open", as the
        @{NoProjectStateScope} says.

    look:
        The tree sits on the darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, a step
        darker than the ribbon's command area, and in light mode a step
        lighter than it instead, #e1e1e1. Each row is 24 pixels tall: an icon, then the
        name 8 pixels after it, in regular text, with no chevrons. Rows start
        16 pixels from the tree's left edge, and each level of a folder's
        contents is indented 24 pixels further, so a file's icon sits beneath
        its folder's name. Clicking a folder's row expands or collapses it.

        A folder shows an outlined folder icon, the same whether it is
        expanded or not. A file shows an outlined text file icon, with lines
        across it; a .pi file's is a
        code file icon, and the project's piton.config.pi a settings file icon
        in the theme's orange. Icons are in muted text colour, except that the
        spec location's folder, as the @{ProjectLocationsScope} says, and its
        .pi files take Spec's colour, and the code location's folder takes
        Code's colour, of the @{PromptModesScope}, each on its icon alone. A
        folder or file whose name starts with a dot, other than a .gitignore
        or similar file, and anything git ignores, is dimmed, name and icon
        both, as tertiary text is; the dimming wins over the name's git status
        colour. The spec and code locations are read from the project's
        piton.config.pi when the project opens, and again whenever its top
        folder is read anew.

        The selected row, the file in the body's selected tab or the folder
        last clicked, has a background of the ribbon's command area colour, #222222
        in dark mode, inset 8 pixels from either side of the tree, with softly
        rounded corners, and its name in semibold. Hovering a row gives it the
        same background, fainter. There are no lines between rows. The
        permanent scrollbar keeps its column at the tree's right, so the
        selected row's background is inset from that column rather than from
        the panel's edge.

    refreshing:
        The tree refreshes by itself when files or folders are added, removed,
        or renamed on disk, keeping expanded folders open and the selection in
        place.

    gitStatus:
        Each name is coloured by its status in the @{GitScope}, in that
        status's color; unchanged names keep the default color, and a folder
        shows the status it takes from its contents, so a change stays visible
        while its folder is collapsed.

    diffButton:
        A new, untracked, or modified file has a small diff button, an icon
        with a "Show the changes" tooltip, at the right end of its row.
        Clicking it opens the file's @{DiffViewScope} rather than the file
        itself.

    opening:
        Clicking a file opens it, as the @{OpenFileScope} says.

    contextMenu:
        Right-clicking a file or folder, or the empty space beneath the rows,
        opens a menu there, with, in order:
        - "New File…", with a file-plus icon, and "New Folder…", with a folder-plus icon: in a folder right-clicked, in the folder holding a file right-clicked, or at the top of the project for the empty space
        - a separator, then "Rename…", with a pencil icon, and "Delete", with a trash icon, for a file or folder only, not the empty space

        Right-clicking a row doesn't open the file or expand the folder.

        The tree has one menu: a right-click opens exactly one, in place of any
        already open, never a row's menu and the empty space's together.
        Choosing from it closes it, and the name then being given keeps the
        focus, rather than the focus going back to whatever had it before the
        menu opened. Closing the menu without choosing gives the focus back.

    naming:
        New File, New Folder, and Rename name what they make or rename in the
        tree itself, inline, where a row's name is: the name is typed over the
        row's label, in the same text size and at the same place, with no box
        of its own taking room, only a thin outline in the theme's ring colour
        just outside it. A row being named is exactly as tall and wide as it
        was, and no other row moves: renaming moves nothing at all, and a new
        file or folder only adds its own row, as tall as any other, at the top
        of its folder, pushing the rows beneath it down by that one row. The
        input has focus, with the name selected for Rename, or empty with a
        placeholder for a new file or folder, the folder expanding to show its
        row. <Enter> makes it so, and <Escape>, or focus moving elsewhere,
        leaves everything as it was.

        A name can't be empty, contain a slash or backslash, be "." or "..", or
        be the name of something already in that folder, other than what is
        being renamed; while it is, the outline is in the theme's error colour,
        a small note just below the row says why, laid over the rows beneath
        rather than moving them, and <Enter> does nothing. If the file system
        refuses, the input stays, saying why the same way.

        A new file is created empty and opens, as the @{OpenFileScope} says. A
        new folder is created, and shown selected. A renamed file or folder
        keeps its place in the tree's order by its new name, stays selected,
        and a folder stays expanded if it was. A file open in a tab that is
        renamed, or is inside a renamed folder, opens again at its new path,
        in the same tab, unless it has unsaved changes, when it stays as it
        is.

    deleting:
        Delete first asks, in a dialog titled "Delete notes.md?" with the name
        of what is deleted, saying it can't be undone, and for a folder, that
        everything in it goes too, with a "Delete" button in the theme's error
        colour and "Cancel". Deleting removes it from disk for good. A file open
        in a tab that is deleted, or is inside a deleted folder, closes, its
        tab with it, without asking about unsaved changes. If the file system refuses, a
        notification titled "Could not delete" says why.

        The tree then refreshes as it does for any change on disk.

#### Changes On Disk

##### Watching

The editor watches its file on disk while it is open, whether or not its tab is selected, and notices when something else edits or renames it: another program, a task, or the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope). Its own saves, the formatting a Piton file gets as it is saved included, are never taken for a change on disk.

##### Reloading

When the file is edited on disk and the editor has no unsaved changes, it reloads at once, without asking, showing the file as it now is on disk. As with saving, the cursor stays at the same place in the text, beside the same characters it was beside, as near as the new text allows, and the view stays scrolled just as it was. The reload can't be undone into the text it replaced, and a Piton file's new text goes to the server as a full-text `textDocument/didChange`.

##### Renaming

When the file is renamed or moved on disk, whether the file system reports it as a rename or the file vanishes while one with the same contents appears in the project at the same moment, the editor follows it to its new path in the same tab: its header shows the new path, its tab the new name and path, and saving writes to the new path. Nothing else about it changes: its text, unsaved changes, cursor, and scrolling stay as they were, so a rename alone never asks anything. A Piton file is closed on the server under its old path with `textDocument/didClose`, and opened under its new one with `textDocument/didOpen`, with the editor's text. A rename that also changes the file's contents is a rename and then an edit.

##### Conflicts

When the file is edited on disk while the editor has unsaved changes, nothing is reloaded. Instead a dialog asks what to do, titled "notes.md changed on disk" with the file's name, saying the file was changed outside the editor while it has unsaved changes here, with three buttons, the last one primary:

- "Keep Mine", which keeps the editor's text as it is, still unsaved, so saving it writes over what is on disk
- "Reload", which discards the unsaved changes and reloads the file as it now is on disk, as reloading says
- "Merge", which opens the merge, as merging says

The dialog shows as soon as the change is noticed, whichever tab is selected, and choosing "Reload" or "Merge" selects the file's tab. <Escape>, or closing the dialog, is "Keep Mine". While the dialog is open, further changes to the file on disk don't open another; the choice made acts on the file as it is on disk when it is made. Each file in conflict gets a dialog of its own, one after another. A file that conflicts again after "Keep Mine" asks again.

##### Merging

##### Watching

When the file is edited on disk and the editor has no unsaved changes, it reloads at once, without asking, showing the file as it now is on disk. As with saving, the cursor stays at the same place in the text, beside the same characters it was beside, as near as the new text allows, and the view stays scrolled just as it was. ##### Renaming

When the file is renamed or moved on disk, whether the file system reports it as a rename or the file vanishes while one with the same contents appears in the project at the same moment, the editor follows it to its new path in the same tab: its header shows the new path, its tab the new name and path, and saving writes to the new path. I've written the spec for this; the code hasn't been touched. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 75 files.

**What changed in the spec**

1. **Editor** (`spec/scope/editor/index.pi`): a new **Changes On Disk** section with four parts:
   - **Watching:** an open file is watched on disk whether or not its tab is selected. The editor's own saves, including the formatting a Piton file gets on save, never count as a change on disk.
   - **Reloading:** if the file is edited on disk and there are no unsaved changes, the editor reloads straight away without asking. The cursor stays beside the same characters and the scroll position doesn't move. A Piton file's new text goes to the language server as a full-text `didChange`.
   - **Renaming:** if the file is renamed or moved on disk, the editor follows it to the new path in the same tab. The header, the tab's name and tooltip, and where saving writes all switch to the new path. Unsaved changes, cursor and scrolling stay as they were, so a rename on its own never asks anything. A Piton file gets `didClose` under the old path and `didOpen` under the new one. A rename that also changes the contents is handled as a rename and then an edit.
   - **Conflicts:** if the file is edited on disk while there are unsaved changes, nothing reloads. A dialog titled "notes.md changed on disk" offers three buttons:
     - "Keep Mine" keeps the editor's text, still unsaved. Escape or closing the dialog does the same.
     - "Reload" discards the unsaved changes and loads the file from disk.
     - "Merge" opens the merge view. It's the primary button.

     "Reload" and "Merge" also select the file's tab. Only one dialog shows per file, files in conflict are asked about one after another, and a file that changes again after "Keep Mine" asks again.
   - **Merging:** the merge view replaces the editor in the file's tab. "Apply Merge" puts the merged text in the editor as unsaved changes; "Cancel" returns to the editor's text as it was.
2. **Diff view** (`spec/ui/components/diff-view/index.pi`): a new **Merging** mode.
   - The left side is the file as it is on disk now, headed "On disk"; the right side is the editor's unsaved text, headed "Mine". It keeps following the file on disk.
   - Each change has "Use Disk" and "Use Mine" buttons, and every change starts on "Use Mine". The side that won't be kept is dimmed, and "Mine" lines that will be replaced are struck through.
   - The header swaps the open-file and close buttons for "Use All Disk", "Use All Mine", "Cancel", and "Apply Merge" as the primary button. Escape is "Cancel".
3. **File tree** (`spec/ui/components/file-tree/index.pi`, Naming): this changes existing behaviour. Before, a file renamed in the tree only moved to its new path if it had no unsaved changes; otherwise it stayed as it was. Now it always follows to the new path and keeps any unsaved changes, matching what the editor does for a rename on disk.

**Anchors the code should follow**
- `.claude/reference/scope/editor/index.md#changes-on-disk` and its sub-anchors `#watching`, `#reloading`, `#renaming`, `#conflicts`, `#merging`
- `.claude/reference/ui/components/diff-view/index.md#merging`, with `#choosing` and `#header` under it
- `.claude/reference/ui/components/file-tree/index.md#naming`
- Unchanged but relevant: the editor's `#saving` (keeping the cursor in place), `#language-support` and `#closing`, and the delete dialog in the file tree's `#deleting` as the pattern for the conflict dialog.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790836506-Prompt_e18179c4cbce5083.understanding.md`.
